column1: # operator-hands-labels.tsv — hand-labelled gate for mesh-operator-hands' prose classifier.
# WHY THESE ARE REPHRASINGS, NOT BOARD LINES. The board (~/.mesh/chat.log) is gitignored and
# carries the operator's mailbox, phone and credentials — it can never be committed as a
# fixture. Every row below is a REDACTED re-phrasing of a real 2026-08-05..16 board line,
# preserving the exact construction the classifier has to read and dropping the identifiers.
# The live board is covered by a SEPARATE --test leg (the fixture cannot cover the live path).
# columns:  label <TAB> kind <TAB> body
#   label  H=hands  W=word  U=dependency-asserted-but-class-undeterminable
#          NONE=names the operator but asserts NO dependency (must not be counted)
#          SKIP=derivative/self line that must be excluded before classification
#   kind   line  = run through the classifier
#          deriv = run through the exclusion filter first (expected SKIP)
# The NONE rows are the teeth: without them the gate could not fail on over-matching, and
# over-matching is exactly how this classifier dies (the operator ACTING reads like the mesh
# WAITING unless the boundary guards hold). Both mutants were run and seen RED before this
# file was committed: dropping the \b(?!ed|ing) guard -> 22/24 (the two NONE rows flip to H/W);
# neutering DERIV_BODY -> 21/24 (all three SKIP rows score).
# FIELD PRECISION IS NOT THIS FILE'S 24/24. Agreement here is a REGRESSION gate on 24 curated
# constructions; it is not the classifier's accuracy on the live board, and quoting it as such
# would be the fixture-flatters-itself trap. A hand audit of the live board on 2026-08-16
# (15 of the 53 hits pulled and read in full context, the ambiguous ones chosen deliberately,
# NOT a random sample) found 4 false positives, all one shape: the operator dependency stated
# about a PAST or third-party matter rather than a live block — "The operator's decision was
# recorded in the genome and the world never adopted it", "a live operator reply lands 10+ min
# late" (a latency defect), "руками оператора" citing the 08-11 wg-mesh incident as an example,
# "retrieval needs the operator's own authenticated session" (why a leaked name is harmless).
# That is ~4/15 on the HARD subset, so the board-wide FP rate is lower — but it is a real and
# UNMEASURED rate, and it biases the count UP. Deliberately not hard-coded into the tool: a
# pinned accuracy constant rots the moment the board's vocabulary moves, and the tool prints
# "audit with --list" instead. Re-run the audit, don't quote this paragraph's number.
